trap-superlative.evidence: 'its mass is the most precisely measured particle mass in the Standard Model' is an unqualified superlative that the numbers in this block's own table do not support: it quotes m_e at 2.9e-10 relative, and CODATA 2018 gives m_p at 3.1e-10 -- the same order, so 'most precisely measured' is at best a tie. It sits inside a three-clause justification ('simplest charged lepton, ... most precisely measured ..., and its brane tower is fully computable'), which is where the inflation is easiest to miss.
trap-superlative.notes: proposed (structural): 'one of the two most precisely measured particle masses' or simply drop the clause -- the other two reasons carry the argument.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: One sentence is truncated mid-clause: 'The free neutron is the simplest hadronic decay -- one crossing change (d -> u) inside one nucleon, no nuclear environment. Once $\mathfrak{E}_0$ is fixed,' and then the text jumps straight to a bold run-in heading '**$\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ cross-check gap.**'. The sentence never completes, so the paragraph has no predicate.
trap-nonspeakable.notes: proposed (structural, NOT applied -- the missing clause is content, not grammar): restore the completion (presumably 'Once E_0 is fixed, every hadronic Q-value follows from (m_e, q_0)' or similar) or delete the fragment. RIGOR (not a trap). VERIFIED OK at the proton-pinned q_0 = 1.1099785827513808: table relative precisions 2.9e-10 / 2.2e-8 / 1.3e-6 all reproduce from the quoted +- values; hbar_q = (q-1)/q agrees with AGENTS.md's 1 - q^{-1}; m_mu/m_e = Vol(4_1)/hbar_q^2 = 206.768326 vs CODATA 206.7682830 (210 ppb, i.e. the documented mu-p tension); Li_2(q^{-2})/hbar_q^2 = 111.90 (quoted ~112) and m_e/that = 4.567e-3 (quoted 4.57e-3); E_0^{(N=0)} = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) = 4.18598 (quoted 4.186); E_0^full = 4.22748 (quoted 4.228); E_0^{(cal)} = 0.78233341/|h(h-2)/2| = 4.17897 (quoted 4.179); h = 0.20906 (quoted 0.209); q/q^{-1} = q^2 = 1.23205 (quoted 1.231); Q_beta(n) = 0.78233341 MeV is exactly m_n - m_p - m_e from CODATA; the 19-parameter Standard-Model count itemises correctly; the typed-decomposition '0.6% gap' measures 0.577%. THREE DEFECTS: (1) NUMERIC BASELINE -- 'With the tower form E_0^full active, the framework-derived value overshoots the calibrated value by +1.75%'. Against the CALIBRATED value defined three paragraphs earlier (4.179) the overshoot is +1.16%; +1.75% is the overshoot against the TYPED-crossings value 4.155, which the block introduces only as a parenthetical alternative. Proposed: name the baseline. (2) ORDERING -- the table lists CAL-1 = m_e first and CAL-2 = m_mu/m_e second, but the prose immediately below says 'The first input is a dimensionless ratio -- it fixes q_0' and 'The second input sets the leptonic mass scale', i.e. the reverse. (3) ABSOLUTE-MASS EXCISION (2026-08-11) -- the Predictions list carries 'Muon mass', 'Proton mass: via Skein pair formula ...' and 'Neutron mass: m_n = m_p + Q_beta' as predictions from q_0 + m_e. Absolute masses are m_e-scaled renderings of ratios and are no longer framework predictions; the muon entry is at least self-labelled '(first prediction, by construction matches calibration input)'. Proposed: restate as m_p/m_e, m_n/m_e and the splitting Delta_pn.
